direct-c-scalar-imports-qbe.summary: `extern def` declarations call fixed-arity C scalar functions directly from QBE native builds.

explicit-native-link-inputs.summary: `mylang build` and `mylang test` accept repeatable object, library and search-path link inputs.

python-free-native-build-driver.summary: `mylang build` drives QBE, the assembler and the linker itself, with no Python installer in the loop.

python-free-native-guest-tests.summary: `mylang test` discovers exported `test_` functions and runs them as fresh native processes.

affected-native-test-result-reuse.summary: A native test run reuses receipts for cases whose sources and compiler identity did not change.

parallel-guest-test-directories.summary: `mylang test` runs a whole directory of `.my` programs as parallel child commands sharing one cache, with one merged summary.

isolated-source-provider-test-fixtures.summary: A test case may replace dependency sources inside a private bounded snapshot that never edits the originals.

guest-performance-benchmarks.summary: `mylang test --bench` measures exported `bench_` workloads against versioned baselines and reviewed policy limits.

keyword-arguments-and-immutable-defaults.summary: Calls accept positional and keyword arguments with trailing immutable scalar defaults.

positional-and-named-record-constructors.summary: A record is constructed by calling its type with positional or named fields.

collection-membership-and-value-equality.summary: `in`, `not in`, `==` and `!=` compare managed collection contents rather than identities.

managed-arenas.summary: `with arena() as name:` releases every managed object allocated during the block in one step.

python-indented-syntax.summary: `def`, `class`, four-space indentation and `#` comments are the source syntax; there is no second spelling.

python-payload-variant-construction.summary: `Shape.radius(4)` builds a payload variant and `case Shape.radius(r)` takes it apart.

python-contextual-array-and-table-litera.summary: A list literal becomes a fixed `[N]T` array and a dict literal an enum-indexed `[Kind]T` table when the context demands one.

python-call-type-arguments.summary: `identity[int](2)` supplies a generic call's type arguments explicitly in Python syntax.

truncating-division-helpers.summary: `divtrunc` and `remtrunc` round toward zero where `//` and `%` round down.

assert-statements.summary: `assert condition` and `assert condition, "message"` trap `R_ASSERT` under every effect bound.

python-string-methods.summary: `str` answers Python's strip, case, search, classification and padding methods with fresh strings.

format-strings.summary: `f"..."` interpolates any value `print` can render, with `{{` and `}}` for literal braces.

list-comprehensions.summary: `[expression for name in source if condition]` builds a managed list in one expression.

wildcard-match-arms.summary: A final `case _` covers every variant no earlier arm named.

prelude-float-operations.summary: Prelude helpers convert, compare and classify binary64 values without importing a module.

python-prelude-builtins.summary: Bare Python `sum`, `min`, `max`, `sorted`, `abs`, `round`, `any`, `all`, `reversed`, `list` and `zip` work without an import.

string-to-number-parsing.summary: `int(text)` and `float(text)` answer `Option` rather than raising on text that is not a number.

python-assignments-and-value-records.summary: Assignment creates a mutable function-scoped local and records keep value semantics on copy.

canonical-prelude-types.summary: `list`, `dict`, `str`, `bytes`, `float`, `Option` and `Result` have one identity in every module without source-text scanning.

inferred-list-literals-and-slices.summary: A list literal infers its element type and `values[a:b]` copies a clamped range into a fresh list.

collection-iteration.summary: `for` visits lists, strings, byte strings and dictionary keys, with `enumerate` for indexes.

managed-unicode-strings.summary: `str` is an immutable garbage-collected sequence of Unicode scalar values.

managed-bytes.summary: `bytes` is an immutable garbage-collected byte string with Python indexing, slicing and search.

managed-insertion-ordered-dictionaries.summary: `dict` keeps insertion order over `int` or `str` keys and copyable values and answers `items`, `pop`, `update`, `setdefault`, `get`, `keys`, `values`, `copy` and `clear`.

dictionary-methods.summary: `dict.pop(key[, fallback])` removes and returns a value, `update` merges another dictionary in insertion order, and `setdefault` returns or stores a fallback.

ordinary-binary64-float.summary: `float` is IEEE binary64 with ordinary literals, operators, comparisons and integer conversions.

contextual-option-constructors.summary: `Some(value)` and a bare `None` take their `Option[T]` type from the surrounding context.

optional-semicolons.summary: A statement ends at a newline; semicolons remain valid for several statements on one line.

dotted-module-qualification.summary: An imported module's exports are named `module.name`, including its types.

builtin-list-and-result-types.summary: `list[T]` and `Result[T, E]` are prelude types that need no declaration or import.

contextual-empty-list-and-result-constru.summary: An empty `[]`, `{}`, `Ok(...)` or `Err(...)` takes its type from the annotation, field or result it fills.

list-methods-and-indexing.summary: Lists answer `append`, `extend`, `insert`, `pop`, `remove`, `index`, `reverse`, `sort`, `copy`, `clear`, `len`, indexing with negative positions and indexed in-place `+=`.

postfix-error-propagation.summary: `expression?` returns a failed `Result` to the caller and unwraps a successful one.

fixed-width-integers.summary: `int` is checked signed 64-bit; `i8`-`i64` and `u8`-`u64` are available for binary formats.

named-integer-bitwise-shifts.summary: `bit_and`, `bit_or`, `bit_xor`, `shift_left` and `shift_right` are named operations over one integer type.

wrapping-saturating-integers.summary: `wrapping_*` reduces modulo the declared width and `saturating_*` clamps to its bounds.

booleans.summary: `True`, `False`, `and`, `or` and `not` are the only condition type; integers do not stand in.

unit-procedures.summary: A procedure omits its return annotation or writes `-> None`, ends naturally or with bare `return`.

byte-literals.summary: `b"..."` and `b'...'` write byte strings with escapes and a decoded-size limit.

nominal-records.summary: `record` declares a nominal value record of annotated fields; `class` remains the compatibility spelling.

tagged-unions.summary: `union` declares a tagged variant type whose cases are matched exhaustively.

checked-results.summary: `Result[T, E]` carries `Ok`/`Err` and must be handled before it is discarded.

generic-functions.summary: `def name[T](...)` declares a template specialized per concrete argument type.

generic-call-argument-inference.summary: A generic call omits its type arguments when the argument types determine every parameter.

const-length-generics.summary: A `const N: u64` parameter carries a bounded array length through generic signatures.

generic-nominals.summary: `class` and `union` declarations take type parameters and specialize by argument identity.

structural-contracts.summary: A generic parameter may require named fields or operations instead of a nominal bound.

capability-effects.summary: A function's declared effect ceiling bounds everything it transitively calls.

disk-modules.summary: A project is `module`/`import`/`export` declarations over files resolved from disk.

typed-json.summary: Exported signatures over JSON-compatible types are checked, rendered by `schema-project`, and carried as `typed-json-v1` test arguments and expectations.

scoped-directory-and-endpoint-providers.summary: The byte runner grants a guest a named directory or network endpoint instead of ambient authority.

scoped-filesystem-metadata-and-listings.summary: Scoped directory providers answer bounded metadata and directory listings.

flexible-top-level-export-placement.summary: `export` may appear anywhere at the top level, before or after the declaration it names.

source-navigation.summary: `index-project` reports definitions, references and a pinned source snapshot as JSON.

syntax-cache.summary: Parsed syntax trees are reused across commands when the source bytes are unchanged.

exact-verdict-cache.summary: A whole-program checking verdict is reused when the compiler and the source snapshot both match.

independent-function-diagnostics.summary: One `check` reports the first fault in each independently checked function instead of stopping at the first.

copied-block-byte-io.summary: The byte host moves data in copied bounded blocks rather than shared buffers.

configurable-byte-io-budgets.summary: Input, output and execution budgets for the byte runner are set on its command line.

scalar-module-constants.summary: `const NAME: T = expression` folds an immutable scalar at check time.

literal-module-constants.summary: String and byte constants require matching literals and allocate on read.

bounded-source-constant-functions.summary: A constant initializer may call bounded nongeneric scalar source functions.

structured-loop-exits.summary: `break` and `continue` leave or restart the nearest enclosing loop with checked cleanup.

integer-range-iteration.summary: `for index in range(start, end)` visits a half-open ascending integer range.

transparent-type-aliases.summary: `type Name = Target` is another spelling for an existing type, not a new identity.

composite-structural-signatures.summary: One structural contract may require several fields and operations together.

local-locked-packages.summary: Imports resolve through a locked local package root with pinned content hashes.

nested-runtime-byte-budgets.summary: Runtime byte budgets nest, so an inner region can never exceed the region containing it.

guest-memory-ceilings.summary: Every process that runs guest code runs under a byte ceiling the heap traps on and the kernel backs with RLIMIT_AS.

native-default-releasefast.summary: `mylang build` and `mylang run` build ReleaseFast unless `--mode Debug` selects an unoptimized binary, and `--report` states the mode.

structured-native-trap-detail.summary: Native traps carry bounded structured index/length and operand detail rendered identically in text and JSON, transported from the child as one versioned stderr record.

symbolic-template-reuse.summary: Checked symbolic generic templates persist direct abstract results under symbolic-template-v1 and replay across processes when the body, dependency context, name-resolution mode and checker version still match; whole-graph effects always rerun.

canonical-specialization-keys.summary: Concrete specialization keys are canonical over template identity, ordered positional descriptors, provider contracts, constraints, declared contracts and build context; validated concrete specialization bodies replay under specialization-v1 with typed remap and conservatively miss on unresolved references.

shared-semantic-retention-budget.summary: Ordinary checked bodies, symbolic templates and concrete specializations share one reuse.max_bytes in-memory budget accounting for exact owned entry rows, arena backing including chunk bookkeeping, stable keys and the exact stdlib hash-index backing; eviction converges to the bound, oversized entries bypass, a zero budget disables reuse, and retained bytes plus a per-kind breakdown are reported.

persistent-checked-bodies.summary: Ordinary checked bodies persist across compiler processes as versioned, validated semantic-cache-v1 entries with atomic publication, remap-or-miss decoding, contract isolation and --no-cache correctness.

native-test-preparation-reuse.summary: A warm unchanged native-test run validates through the shared query cache, reuses closure-bound result receipts and executes zero tests without lowering, emitting or linking; durable checked facts key fully cached selections, and a miss lowers, emits and links only the selected tests' reachable closure.

selected-test-providers.summary: Native test preparation validates exported declaration contracts first and fully checks only the selected replacement provider graph; replacements must satisfy every public contract they replace, and receipts bind contract, provider and source identities.

required-project-import-policy.summary: A discovered entry-anchored mylang.json makes its import_policy required for ordinary check, build, run, project and native-test commands before any cached success, with config and policy identity in receipts.

checked-mutation-contracts.summary: effects(mutation) with mutates(...) permits only declared caller-owned managed writes; deep origins, return aliasing and conservative overlap rejection are checked through calls, generics and callbacks.

per-function-body-reuse.summary: Ordinary checked bodies reuse per function with stable declaration identities and dependency digests, so an unrelated generic, alias, constant or callback no longer disables reuse.

actual-work-report.summary: Versioned work-report-v1 separates unchanged fingerprints from actual result reuse and reports per-stage performed, reused and skipped work with bypass reasons and session deltas.

native-instruction-and-frame-budgets.summary: `--max-steps=N` and `--max-frames=N` impose opt-in instruction and call-depth ceilings on an otherwise unbounded guest run, and each trap names the flag that raises it.

memory-bounded-test-fanout.summary: A directory test run sizes its worker pool from free memory as well as cores, with --jobs and MYLANG_JOBS to override it.

typed-holes.summary: `todo[T]()` declares an unfinished implementation with a checked type and blocks publication.

named-executable-laws.summary: A named law is an executable property statement checked with the rest of the suite.

deterministic-test-provider-fixtures.summary: A guest test runs with no ambient authority, and a case may replace a dependency's source to make a reading deterministic.

typed-noncapturing-function-values.summary: A function value has a declared signature and captures nothing.

expression-bodied-lambdas.summary: A contextually typed `lambda` spells an expression-bodied noncapturing callback.

bounded-guest-callbacks.summary: A callback parameter declares its signature and an effect ceiling; an implementation callable may use a subset of the destination's effects.

changed-source-function-body-cache.summary: Unchanged function bodies reuse their checked results when other functions in the module change.

managed-lists.summary: `list[T]` is a growing garbage-collected sequence shared by assignment.

nonmoving-tracing-gc.summary: A single-threaded nonmoving tracing collector reclaims managed objects at allocation safepoints.

managed-list-cycles.summary: Cyclic managed graphs are reclaimed; reference counting only protects temporary roots.

standard-math.summary: `math` provides classification, rounding, roots, powers and integer helpers over `float` and `int`.

standard-strings.summary: `strings` provides classification, search, trimming, padding and number formatting over `str`.

standard-sort.summary: `sort` provides stable ordering, binary search, extrema and deduplication over managed lists.

standard-path.summary: `path` joins, splits and normalizes POSIX-style path text without touching the filesystem.

standard-hex.summary: `hex` encodes and decodes hexadecimal text for byte strings in either letter case.

standard-base64.summary: `base64` encodes and decodes standard and URL-safe base64 text.

standard-json.summary: `json` parses and renders ordinary JSON documents as a bounded managed tree.

standard-pool.summary: `pool` provides generation-checked handles into a reusable slot table.

standard-random.summary: `random` provides a deterministic SplitMix64 stream seeded explicitly or from an entropy capability.

standard-time.summary: `time` provides durations, instants and Unix wall-clock readings behind a clock capability.

doc-examples.summary: Every fenced documentation example is run, type-checked or explicitly skipped by the default gate.

python-print-and-output-effect.summary: `print` renders values Python-style and contributes an `output` effect.

python-file-surface.summary: `with open(...)`, handle methods and whole-path helpers read and write inside granted directories.

command-line-capability-grants.summary: `mylang run` grants every capability by default; `--restrict` denies them and `--allow-*` narrows what it grants back.

documented-feature-coverage.summary: `mylang doc-coverage` fails the build when an implemented feature or a standard export has no documented example.

named-constraints.summary: `constraint Name[Subject] = ...` names a reusable structural requirement shared by function type parameters.

stable-incremental-identities.summary: Compiler identities for modules, declarations, bodies, types, specializations and emitted fragments are content-derived and stable across unrelated edits.

invalidation-report.summary: `--explain-invalidation` reports per-stage hit/miss and the first changed dependency against a stored baseline; `--report` adds per-stage counts.

incremental-cache-contract.summary: Incremental cache keys include compiler identity, bootstrap version, target, runtime ABI, effects/capabilities contract and flags.

clean-warm-invalidation-matrix.summary: A clean-versus-warm invalidation matrix proves status, diagnostics, interface manifest, QBE and reuse counts agree.

limits.generic_calls: explicit arguments or complete inference from call inputs; ambiguous and unmaterialized phantom arguments require explicit specialization
limits.unit: unit/None procedures; main accepts int, unit, or Result[int/unit,int]; copied host/JSON unit signatures remain excluded
limits.container_elements: managed list/dict elements: copyable values without must-handle obligations, owned resources, or capability grants
limits.iteration: range(end/start,end), list/str/dict foreach and enumerate; fixed bounds and structural mutation checks
limits.native_runtime: QBE only; host effects require explicit ABI registration
limits.workers: no host worker facility and no guest spawn syntax; parallelism is one guest process per task
limits.floating_point: float literals, ordinary operators, signed int conversions; IEEE binary64; standard sqrt is the correctly rounded binary64 operation, decimal parsing is accurate rather than correctly rounded; no transcendentals
limits.callbacks: generic signatures, exact effect ceilings, explicit readonly context borrows, no captures or reference results
limits.semantic_reuse: ordinary checked bodies and concrete specializations replay across processes; symbolic templates keep abstract checking; unresolved nested or interned-identity references stay conservative; in-memory retention is bounded by one shared reuse.max_bytes budget and a zero budget disables reuse
limits.text_data: managed Unicode scalar strings and managed bytes; host byte I/O keeps its scalar ABI
limits.time_random: Unix wall clock and explicit entropy capabilities; deterministic noncryptographic SplitMix64
limits.managed_lists: copyable shared aliases; automatic growth; no owned/resource elements, borrowed interiors, untraced storage embedding, or host escape
limits.gc: single-threaded nonmoving tracing; retained guest values root intermediates; collect-on-allocation stress option
limits.python: static fixed-width types, function-scoped locals with E_UNBOUND definite assignment, value records; indentation is the only block syntax
limits.dictionaries: managed insertion order; homogeneous int or str keys and copyable values
limits.native_tests: fresh QBE processes; exported typed-call-compatible signatures; positive deterministic receipts only; project validity is always checked through the shared query cache; only a fully cached selection skips lowering/emission/linking, while a changed snapshot still pays one whole-project preparation emission and an uncached selection builds the whole selected-provider library; provider snapshots at most 128 sources/16 MiB
limits.standard_library: ten embedded Python-syntax modules over managed types: math, strings, sort, path, hex, base64, json, pool, random, time

explicit-storage-tier.note: buffer/pool/list declarations, the allocator capability, references and slices, lexical borrows, legacy arena scopes and every standard module built on them. Managed collections and `with arena()` regions replace them.

c-backend.note: emit-c/emit-project-c, src/native.zig and the C-only runtime. QBE is the only native backend.

record-literals-without-new.note: merged into positional-and-named-record-constructors; the `new T { ... }` spelling it was named against left with the legacy brace syntax.

legacy-migration.note: mylang migrate/migrate-project, src/migrate*.zig and their drivers. Their input was the brace dialect, which no longer exists.

legacy-syntax.note: the brace dialect: fn/let/let mut/struct/new, `T { … }` record literals, `::` qualification, `::<T>` turbofish, `cast<T>(x)`, `//` comments, `{ }` scope blocks, match expressions, `true`/`false`/`unit`, `else if` and `a..b` ranges. Indentation, `def`/`class`, `T(f=v)`, `alias.name`, `f[T](x)`, `T(x)`, `#` comments, `match`/`case`, `True`/`False`/`None`, `elif` and `range(a, b)` are the surface.

value-producing-matches.note: `match e { P => v }` had only a brace spelling and no Python one; a `match` statement whose arms return covers the same programs.

bounded-scalar-source-evaluation.note: the eval-project command, its step/frame/eval-byte budgets and its eval-report-v1 / evaluation-request documents. It executed a parameter-free entry in the compiler's own process; `mylang run` builds the program natively and runs it instead.

bounded-vm-trace.note: vm_trace.Trace and the vm.Options.memory.trace hook. The ring of recent instructions it sampled was an interpreter artifact; a native guest reports a source-mapped call stack at its trap instead.

in-memory-host-replay.note: host_replay.Transcript and its recorded call comparison. It wrapped an interpreter provider registration, and a natively built guest calls its registered provider directly.

isolated-process-workers.note: scripts/workers.py and its typed-call-v1 job pool. Each job dispatched one guest call through invoke-project; nothing replaces it, and the language still has no spawn syntax.

memory-accounting-categories.note: mylang-io --memory-report, --max-runtime-bytes, --max-vm-bytes and --max-host-bytes, and the runtime-memory-v1 split of VM bytes into guest backing and bookkeeping. There is no VM allocator to split; guest-memory-ceilings bounds a guest process instead.
